tara: quick report from today's calypso-lite-int6 bringup: small but consistent regressions in the multiorient subtitle smoke. two different symptoms: 1) CJK vertical lines showing punctuation (brackets/quotes) glued to ideographs causing column misalignment, 2) Hebrew/Arabic bracket mirroring flips in rendered output. repro below. :mag:
vikram: please paste the exact eval command and a tiny failing snippet so we can reproduce locally.
tara: running: `rrun eval --model=calypso-lite-int6 --suite=multiorient_subtiles --subset=zh_vertical,hebrew_rtl --shards=1 --jobs=4 --log-token-ids --log-detok`

quick summary:
``
zh_vertical: BLEU baseline=30.0 -> calypso-int6=24.1 (regressions 82/300)
hebrew_rtl: bracket-mirror flips baseline=0 -> calypso-int6=19/300
en_subs: stable
```

tara: minimal zh example input: "（中国）
"
baseline detok tokens: ["（","\u4e2d\u56fd","\uff09"]
int6 detok tokens:   ["（\u4e2d\u56fd\uff09"]  # opening bracket fused to ideograph -> vertical column shift

sofia: do token ids change? tokenizer edits would be surprising.
tara: token ids are identical between good/bad runs for the failing shard. snippet: `token_ids=[121,4433,77]` for both. but rendered layout differs.

leo: packaging note: calypso-int6 changed kernel pack to packed-attn-quant and enabled per-head quant-scale folding plus a new kvcache compaction heuristic. nothing touched tokenizer config. this matches other int6 anomalies we've seen.
vikram: identical ids + different rendering usually points at downstream shaping or hidden-state sensitive detok steps. compaction can alter when KVs are evicted and slightly change attention distribution. that small drift can flip whether a ZERO WIDTH JOINER/SPACE is emitted or how bidi shaping treats bracket pairs.
sofia: can we A/B with `--no-kvcache-compaction --force-stable-quant`? if that fixes it then compaction+quant fold interaction is suspicious.
tara: ran a quick A/B on 200 samples: compaction off + stable-quant lowers zh regressions to 7/200 and hebrew flips to 0/200. compaction on alone reduces but not fully.

leo: interesting. identical token ids but different decode visuals implies the detokenizer or bidi postprocess sees different hidden/context signals. we should collect per-token attention mass diffs for the bracket/quote tokens. small shifts can change class decisions.
vikram: I ran a hidden-state diff for an affected case: L2 deltas per-token are tiny (~1e-3) but attention mass redistributed by ~10% toward the ideograph token when compaction triggers early. that correlates with emitting a fused subtoken during detok and with altered bidi shaping.
sofia: practical next steps: 1) add a tiny locale-focused smoke test to the onboard suite that checks zh-vertical punctuation separation and RTL bracket orientation for any new int6 candidate; 2) make kvcache compaction conservative for mixed-orientation scripts (heuristic detection at request time); 3) introduce a build flag `--quant-stability-mode` to disable per-head folding during early canaries; 4) run kernel-only revert (packed-attn-quant -> packed-attn) to confirm kernel interaction.
tara: uploaded a minimal repro to evals: `/evals/smoke/multiorient/calypso_zwj_rtl_repro_1801112222.txt` and rendered PNGs under `/evals/smoke/renders/1801112222/` for UX.
comp-bot: canary job queued: calypso-int6-multiorient-canary #91207 (compaction=false)
vikram: I'll open a bisect ticket and include the hidden-state diffs and a small script to compute attention mass shifts. ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/BR-1890 (brief: int6 kvcache compaction + per-head fold -> multiorient layout drift)
sofia: thanks. I'll PR the CI smoke test first so we catch this earlier, and add a short runbook note about `quant-stability-mode` for eng-runtime oncall. :memo:
